title: Dynamic evaluation protocol for config-change attribution and rubric blending
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Why: We frequently observe small but actionable quality regressions after non-model config changes (quantization profile, kernel toggle, batch size defaults). Current evals compare global baselines and use a single rubric, which conflates model drift and config-induced variability. This ticket scopes a protocol to attribute QA changes to config vs model, and to blend rubric signals across cohorts so decisioning during rollouts is less brittle.

What: Define and ship a dynamic evaluation protocol that includes: a) per-config synthetic control cohorts using lightweight counterfactual prompt perturbations, b) a rubric-blending layer that weights LLM-as-judge outputs by cohort-level calibration, and c) automated alerts with attribution tags for rollout guardrails. The goal is to reduce false positive regressions and improve root-cause fidelity for on-call and product owners.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol doc (Confluence) with experiment recipes and analysis checklist published and reviewed by Research and Eng
Eval harness changes merged that produce per-config cohort metrics and cohort-weighted rubric scores (CI tests + example run)
Dashboard tile in Console showing attributed regression signals (model vs config) and top contributing prompts/cohorts
Rollout gating rule prototype that blocks canary promotion on high-confidence config-attributed quality drop is exercised on an internal experiment
notes: Key idea: create short paired prompt perturbations (semantic-preserving edits + templated corner cases) to elicit sensitivity to runtime config changes while holding model weights constant.
Rubric blending: combine a small ensemble of LLM-as-judge calls with a calibration model that rescales scores per-cohort based on historical disagreement vs human adjudication.
We plan to reuse existing eval harness infra (evals-harness) and extend output schema with 'attribution' tags and 'cohort_id'.
Consideration: chain-of-thought style judge prompts inflate variance; we will include a lightweight judge prompt set optimized for calibration stability.
Risk: Overfitting attribution heuristics to internal workloads. Mitigation: hold out external customer prompt layers and validate on two enterprise datasets.
decisions: Use counterfactual prompt pairs as the primary mechanism for config-sensitive cohorts (agreed 2026-02-20 meeting)
Adopt temperature-anchored judge prompts (T=0.1) for ensemble members to reduce aleatoric judge noise
Score blending will be multiplicative: cohort_weight * judge_score + (1-cohort_weight) * baseline_signal, where cohort_weight derived from historical calibration error
Initial rollout gating to mark signals as 'config-attributed' only when cohort attribution probability > 0.7 and observed delta > 1.5 stddev
